questions.prompt: A plugin's pre-execute listener returns allow without calling next. A later listener would deny the call. What happens?
options: The later listener still runs and denies the call
The later listener never runs, so the call is allowed unless a guard refuses it
The harness runs the call twice
The harness throws an error because next was not called
questions.explanation: In a waterfall, skipping next stops every listener after it. Guards still run after the chain, which is why a final refusal belongs in a guard.

questions.prompt: Why can a pre-execute listener not rewrite a call's arguments?
options: Because arguments are too large to copy
Because the model would not notice the change
Because the call is already recorded exactly as the model wrote it, and a rewrite would make the record wrong
questions.explanation: The arguments are already in the record. Changing them later would make the record disagree with what ran, so a listener can only allow, deny or ask.

questions.prompt: What can a guard function return?
options: A reason to refuse, or undefined to leave the call as it is
questions.explanation: A guard has no allow answer. It only refuses or abstains, so no ordering of plugins can turn its refusal into permission.
